learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will discover the difference between Main and Helping verbs, and learn to identify Transitive and Intransitive verbs based on objects.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Verbs are the action heroes of grammar! But did you know some heroes work alone, while others need a trusty sidekick? Let's meet the Main Verbs and their Helping Verbs! 🦸‍♂️

lesson_modules.module_title: ⭐ Main Verbs and Helping Verbs (The Sidekicks)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: The Main Verb shows the actual action (run, eat, sleep). Helping Verbs come before the main verb to help show the time (tense) of the action. Common helpers are: is, am, are, was, were, has, have, had, do, does, did.
examples_or_templates: She is running. ('is' = helping verb, 'running' = main verb)
They have finished the homework. ('have' = helping verb, 'finished' = main verb)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Transitive Verb is an action that is passed on to a receiver, called an Object. It needs an object to make complete sense. Ask 'What?' or 'Whom?' after the verb to find the object.
examples_or_templates: The boy kicked the ball. (Kicked what? The ball. 'Ball' is the object, so 'kicked' is transitive.)
She wrote a letter. (Wrote what? A letter.)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: An Intransitive Verb does NOT pass the action to an object. It makes complete sense on its own. If you ask 'What?' or 'Whom?' after the verb, you won't get an answer.
examples_or_templates: The baby slept. (Slept what? No answer. 'Slept' is intransitive.)
The stars shine brightly. (Shine what? 'Brightly' is how, not what!)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the helping verb in this sentence: 'The children were playing outside.'
❓ Is the verb in 'The glass broke.' Transitive or Intransitive?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the helping verb and circle the main verb: 'I have finished my painting.'
subjective_practice.hint: Which word is the main action, and which word is assisting it?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Find the object in this sentence to prove the verb is transitive: 'The dog chewed the bone.'
subjective_practice.hint: Ask the question: The dog chewed WHAT?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write one sentence using the verb 'run' as an Intransitive verb.
subjective_practice.hint: Just tell us who ran and how/where, but don't add a 'what'!

activity_or_assignment.title: 🔍 Verb Detective Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down 5 actions you did today (e.g., ate breakfast, laughed). Next to each one, write whether the action was Transitive (had an object) or Intransitive (no object)!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Helping verbs (is, have, did) assist the Main verb to show tense.
⭐ Transitive verbs need an object to receive the action (read a book).
⭐ Intransitive verbs do NOT need an object and make sense on their own (the baby cried).
